# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

Declined checkout payments aren't stored anywhere locally, so I'll need an additive PaymentAttempt store that captures payment_intent.payment_failed and succeeded events, including decline code, card brand/country, method type, and 3DS flag. I should check whether the webhook actually subscribes to payment_intent events.

Since only payment_failed is confirmed configured, I'll rely on WalletTransaction and Invoice records for successes, and add a PaymentEvent table for failures. I should verify that last_payment_error.payment_method includes the expanded card brand/country data — it does, since Stripe expands that object in the webhook payload.

I also want to check whether off-session renewal failures (dunning) in worker/billing are handled separately, and whether I should record PaymentEvent there too — I'll look for dunningStage logic to confirm. Given the scope, I'll keep this minimal: a small helper function that performs a raw SQL insert and never throws, called from both the webhook failure handler and the off-session failure path, then plan out the schema changes needed.

For the schema, I'm adding ErrorDaily, PaymentEvent, and ReportView tables, and deciding to skip rollup snapshots in favor of live SQL queries with proper indexing, since production data volume (under 1000 users, tens of thousands of visits) is small enough that live queries should perform well. I'm sketching the reports module structure: a range utility supporting timezone-aware boundaries via IANA tz and Intl, an aggregation layer using raw SQL to build per-domain metric structs, a pure rules engine comparing current/previous/baseline periods into findings, and a narrative renderer turning findings into summary sentences.

I'm also planning friction detection rules within the engine, a per-customer journey timeline module, admin pages for reports and journeys, a CSV export route, a print-friendly view, saved views via server actions, and a settings toggle for an off-by-default digest worker that runs daily/weekly. For testing, I'm outlining engine, range, and aggregate test files against a seeded throwaway database plus an RBAC test, and I need to check what test framework the project already uses.

137 /root/agent-notes/signup-friction/REPORT.md
# Signup journey and friction, last 7 days (2026-09-29 to 10-06) vs previous 7 and previous 30

Read-only analysis (prod DB SELECT, journalctl, nginx, code). Internal QA accounts (nxeon-internal.test, nxeon.local) excluded
from rates; one QA account generated 35 of the 49 game provision errors and 79 of 93 game "complete" events this week.
No customer-identifying data is written here. Cohort = CUSTOMER accounts created in the window.

## Summary

Signups rose 56 percent week over week (150 real vs 96; previous-30-day average is 21/day, this week 21.6/day, last week 13.7/day).
The growth is almost entirely cold, free-intent traffic: 60 percent of this week's signups were ChatGPT-attributed
(utm_source=chatgpt.com, vs 26 percent last week), 58 landed first on /free-vps and 28 on /free-minecraft, and 45 percent are
Mobile (Android 41 percent), up from 33 percent. Those segments almost never buy: the 83 signups from /free-vps over two weeks
produced 0 servers and 0 paid top-ups; the 28 from /free-minecraft produced 0 and 0; mobile signups this week produced 0 servers
and 0 paid top-ups from 68 (1 server from 32 the week before). Because of that mix, the signup-to-order rate looks worse this week
(9 percent have a server vs 7 percent, but wizard-open fell to 56 percent from 69 percent and "reached Payment" fell to 23 percent
from 44 percent), even though the product itself (provisioning, wizard) is working: 23 of 23 new-user servers are RUNNING, the median
order-to-"deployed email" time is about 4.5 minutes, and card/Stripe top-ups are succeeding. The money friction is therefore
(1) acquisition-promise mismatch ("free VPS" pages vs no free VPS), (2) mobile wizard drop, (3) Payment-step abandonment, concentrated
in India/Indonesia/Singapore/Bangladesh, with no instrumentation to see why, and (4) post-signup activation (free Minecraft servers that
nobody connects to). Nothing in the Oct 5-6 deploys shows up as a new customer-facing regression; the 15:23 UTC crash cost about 5 minutes
and 29 /login 502s.

## Funnel (real accounts, users)

| Stage | Prev 30d (14-44d ago) | Prev 7d | This 7d |
|---|---|---|---|
| Signups | 627 (20.9/day) | 96 | 150 |
| Google sign-in share | 70% | 76% | 79% |
| Email signups verified (of email signups) | n/a | 16 of 23 (70%) | 23 of 31 (74%) |
| Opened any deploy wizard | 507 (81%) | 66 (69%) | 84 (56%) |
|  of which VPS / game / hosting / email | | 36/37/10/3 | 47/45/3/5 |
| Reached the Payment step | 133 (21%) | 42 (44%) | 34 (23%) |
| Has any server (incl. admin-granted/free) | 24 (3.8%) | 7 (7.3%) | 14 (9.3%) |
| Real paid top-up (Stripe or PayPal) | 26 (4.1%) | 9 (9.4%) | 9 (6.0%) |
| Returned 1+ day after signup | n/a | 15 (16%) | 23 (15%) |
| Returned 1+ day, owners of a server | | 4 of 7 | 9 of 14 (64%) |
| Returned 1+ day, non-owners | | 11 of 89 (12%) | 14 of 136 (10%) |

Session-level wizard steps (all visitors, QA excluded, steps used since the Sep 14 wizard rewrite):

| Wizard | Step | Prev 7d | This 7d |
|---|---|---|---|
| VPS | Configure | 60 | 59 |
|  | Region | 45 | 29 |
|  | Payment | 44 | 27 |
|  | Completed (events) | 5 | 2 |
| Game | Game | 50 | 48 |
|  | Server (plan) | 43 | 49 |
|  | Region | 26 | 22 |
|  | Payment | 24 | 19 |
|  | Completed (events) | 7 | 14 (about 11 users) |

Cohort mix, this week vs last: ChatGPT 91 vs 25 signups; Google organic 24 vs 39; direct 13 vs 5. Desktop 72 vs 58; Mobile 68 vs 32.
Top countries this week: India 16, Brazil 9, Germany 9, US 9, Indonesia 8, Philippines 5, Bangladesh 5, Vietnam 5, Mexico 5, Pakistan 5.
Brazil and Mexico are new in the top list (last week they were not in the top 10). Self-reported source ("heard about us", 150 users): ChatGPT 37, Google 12,
YouTube 5, 80 skipped. Partner program: referral clicks 101 this week vs 8 last week, 7 converted to a signup, 8 PartnerCustomer rows.

By segment (this week + last, real accounts):

| Segment | Signups | Opened wizard | Reached Payment | Has server | Paid |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop | 130 | 86 | 52 | 19 | 16 |
| Mobile | 100 | 57 | 22 | 1 | 2 |
| Landed on /free-vps | 83 | 53 | 21 | 0 | 0 |
| Landed on /free-minecraft (this week only) | 28 | 8 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| ChatGPT-attributed, this week | 91 | 51 | 19 | 7 | 6 |
| ChatGPT-attributed, last week | 25 | 20 | 15 | 1 | 1 |
| Google organic (this week + last) | 63 | 41 | 23 | 5 | 4 |

## Top friction points (ranked)

### 1. Free-intent landing pages bring signups that cannot convert (project, but the copy change is quick)
- 83 /free-vps signups in 14 days, 0 servers, 0 paid. 28 /free-minecraft signups this week, 0 servers, 0 paid.
- The page itself says "nobody gives a real VPS away; there is no free tier" but the title/H1/URL ("Free VPS", "Start free") pull in people searching for a free VPS. Page title: "Free VPS: start free, no credit card". The sign-up credit is 0 for all 150 new users (signupCreditCents is 0), so "claim any free-credit offer" has nothing behind it.
- Fix: (quick) change the /free-vps hero to state what is actually free (free Minecraft server, no card to sign up) and show the price of the cheapest paid server in the hero; add a first-visit "starter credit" if the owner wants this traffic to convert; track /free-vps visitors separately in the admin dashboard so these signups do not mask real conversion. (project) decide whether ChatGPT-sourced "free" queries are the audience to chase; they generate signups but not revenue, which is consistent with the earlier finding that conversion (not traffic) is the bottleneck.

### 2. Mobile signups never reach a server (project)
- 68 mobile signups this week: 35 opened a wizard, 10 reached Payment, 0 ordered, 0 paid (week before: 32, 22, 12, 1, 2).
- Game wizard on mobile: 25 users hit step 1, 18 hit Server, only 5 reach Region and 5 Payment; desktop is 49, 48, 25, 24. So game wizard loses mobile users between Server (plan) and Region (28 percent proceed vs 52 percent on desktop). VPS: Configure 34 mobile to Region 18.
- Android is 62 of 150 signups (Mobile Chrome 54); iOS is only 9.
- Fix: audit /dashboard/deploy on a 390 px Android viewport (plan cards, region step, sticky continue button, keyboard covering the CTA, long single-column scroll); consider a "continue on desktop" link or email-me-this-config at the Payment step. Add a mobile/desktop split to /admin/deploy-funnel. Project (1-2 days).

### 3. Payment step abandonment with no visibility into why (quick instrumentation, then fix)
- 34 users reached Payment this week; 9 paid (26 percent). Last week 42 and 9 (21 percent), prior 30 days 133 and 26.
- Reached-Payment-to-paid by country (two weeks): India 7 reached, 1 paid; Indonesia 5 and 0; Singapore 6 and 0; Bangladesh 3 and 0; Iran 2 and 0; Netherlands 2 and 0; vs Philippines 3 of 7 and Vietnam 3 of 5, Malaysia 2 of 2, Australia 2 of 2.
- The data cannot say why. Payment goes through hosted Stripe Checkout and PayPal; the app logs nothing for card declines, 3DS failures, abandoned Checkout sessions or currency problems, and DeployFunnelEvent has no "checkout opened", "checkout cancelled", or "payment failed" event type (only 3 hosting "ORDER_ERROR"s and one VPS "impersonating" error appear at the Payment step). Web logs show only one Stripe error pattern, "[cards] detach failed ... not attached to a customer" (7 occurrences), and 2 "PaymentMethod previously used without Customer" transient billing errors on a renewal. PayPal: 3 PENDING gameOrder and 3 PENDING order that never completed in Sept 20-30 plus one "account not vault-enabled" fallback warning per restart.
- Fix: (quick) add events checkout_opened / checkout_cancelled / checkout_return(success) and a Stripe webhook handler that writes payment_intent.payment_failed with decline_code and country into DeployFunnelEvent or ErrorLog; (quick) confirm the local-methods endpoint (UPI, GrabPay, FPX, etc.) is surfaced for India/Indonesia/Singapore/Bangladesh at the Payment step; (project) wallet-minimum / first-month price display in local currency for the emerging markets that make up 50 to 60 percent of signups.

### 4. Free Minecraft activation gap (quick to investigate, medium to fix)
- 40 free Minecraft servers were created by new users in 14 days (33 this week; median 1.9 minutes after signup, so the create flow is fast). Only 6 of 40 (15 percent) were ever woken by a player, only 1 reached real multiplayer. Upsell was shown 22 times, clicked 4, and 1 of the 40 owners later bought a paid server.
- Chat topics from new users: "How do I invite my Bedrock player", "how to make it bedrock", "My Minecraft server is offline ... The VM must be running to control the game service" (Oct 4), "From where I can manage my server", "I cant connect to my server" (ticket). Sign that "how to connect and invite a friend" is the first-hour question.
- Fix: after create, show connect address (Java and Bedrock), copy button, "send to a friend" share link, and a "waiting for first player" state; add the first-wake nudge email at +30 min if nobody has connected. Quick win with a high effect on the 21 percent of new users who take this path.

### 5. Game-port verification failures and stale provisioning state (Bedrock fix shipped; verify)
- Real customers' game provisions failed with "game port N never opened ... ECONNREFUSED after ~307 s" 12 times in 14 days (Minecraft 25565 x2, Valheim 2456 x4 on node 178.63.94.114, CS-style 27015 x2, and Bedrock 19132/udp x3 on Oct 6 04:00-05:31 UTC across two nodes, before the 05:24 Bedrock TRANSPORT=raknet commit reached prod at 05:34 and a customer retried). Failure emails (`server_provision_failed`) went to 3 new users on Oct 1 (38 mails, most for QA servers) and 2 on Oct 2.
- None of the new-user servers is in ERROR; all 23 are RUNNING and order-to-deployed email is 2 to 10 minutes except Rust 4 GB (24.5 min) and Left 4 Dead 2 (29.5 min).
- Two new-user servers (Valheim 8 GB and Project Zomboid 8 GB, both Oct 2) show status RUNNING but provisioningStep still reads "Installing the game, this one is a large download..." 4.6 days later and no `server_deployed` email ever sent: the customer is never told the game is ready, and the step text is stale. Quick fix: clear provisioningStep on first successful A2S/port check and send the deployed email; add a watchdog for RUNNING servers with a non-empty provisioningStep older than 30 minutes.
- Fix: verify the Bedrock fix with a real Bedrock order on staging; alert when a real customer sees a PROVISION_FAILED event (currently only visible in the funnel table).

### 6. Capacity refusals for large VPS configs (quick to confirm, project to fix)
- ErrorLog and web logs: "RAM guard refused node-5, node-2, node-4 for a 32768 MB VM" 96 times Oct 2-6; "...node-5, node-2, node-4, node-6 for a 52224 MB VM" 7 times on Oct 6 (so node-6 is enabled but still full or ineligible for that size); "node-2, node-4 for a 16384 MB VM" 26; "node-4 for a 4096 MB VM" 43 (Oct 1 to Oct 6, including 14 on Oct 6). These errors carry no userId, so I cannot confirm they are customers. One new customer's Custom 6 vCPU / 32 GB VPS was finally created at 14:01 UTC Oct 6 after refusals from 05:17 through 13:45, which is consistent with a customer retrying for about 8 hours.
- Customer-visible effect is a generic failure in the wizard rather than "sold out" copy. Fix: surface a clear "this size is temporarily unavailable in region X, try Y" with a notify-me option; log the userId on refusals so they can be counted.

### 7. Mid-session breakage after deploys and a handful of 5xx on customer paths (quick)
- "Failed to find Server Action" (stale client after a deploy) appeared 253 times, 231 on Oct 1 (deploy day); client errors "Loading chunk N failed" about 30 over two weeks; React `removeChild` errors in the dashboard 41 (typical of browser translation/extensions, 4 browsers), "An error occurred in the Server Components render" 27.
- nginx 5xx on real customer paths this week: /login 502 x29 on Oct 6 (crash window 15:23-15:28 UTC, 60 502s in the hour), x9 Oct 3, x6 Oct 1; /dashboard/servers/* 502 x48; /dashboard/support 500 x45 on Oct 4 16:xx; /api/chat/upload 500 x22 (Oct 1 14:xx). No 500 on /dashboard/deploy or /register in the week.
- Fix: serve a "new version available, refresh" prompt on server-action failure (the deploy wizard in particular); investigate Oct 4 /dashboard/support 500s and Oct 1 chat upload 500s.

### 8. Hosting wizard validation dead-end and miscellaneous (quick)
- Hosting wizard: "Enter a valid domain (e.g. example.com)." fired twice on step Payment (Sept 26 and 27), i.e. the user got all the way to checkout before the domain was validated. Move validation to the Domain step. Hosting accounts for 3 of 84 wizard users this week, so this is low priority.
- Verification: 8 of 31 email signups this week never verified (15 users overall across two weeks); 10 of those 15 used the deploy wizard anyway, so verification is not blocking them. The verification link redirected to https://0.0.0.0:3000 until the fix at Oct 5 02:26 UTC reached prod (Oct 5 10:50 release); users who clicked it before then saw a broken page. Email-verify opens 19 of 36 (53 percent); clicks are not tracked on verify links.

## Win-back and other lifecycle emails
- deploy_winback: 121 distinct recipients in 14 days (69 this week); 17 opened (14 percent), 5 clicked (4 percent), 31 returned to the site, 5 ordered something afterwards and 2 topped up, 0 redeemed COMEBACK50. Marketing mail is working technically but is not moving revenue; the 50 percent offer is not the lever for this audience.
- server_deployed: 74 sent, 22 opened. invoice_new 107 sent, 15 opened (14 percent).

## Notable individual cases (masked)
- Customer h***: Bedrock server failed at 19132/udp three times on Oct 6 morning (two nodes), asked in chat how to invite a Bedrock player; likely the NetherNet default bug fixed at 05:34. Worth a proactive "fixed, redeploy" note once ticket replies are approved (no replies sent by this analysis).
- Customer z***: Valheim at 2456/udp on node 178.63.94.114 failed three times Oct 1, then succeeded on the 8 GB plan; two 8 GB servers (Valheim, Project Zomboid, Oct 2) still show the "large download" step text 4.6 days on, no ready email.
- Customer f***: 27015 (Source-engine) game failed twice Oct 2 within 40 minutes, then retried; a real customer hitting repeated failures like this is the case worth a proactive follow-up.
- Customer c*** (Sept 4 signup): "PVE POST .../qemu/657/config -> 403 Permission check failed" at game provision, Oct 4: a Proxmox token-permission failure on a node (not a customer mistake); same family as the known split-token item.
- A new-user ticket "Server cannot be created" (Oct 1) and "VPS web-01 stuck in ERROR state" (Sep 28): both closed; one failed dedicated-IP purchase was refunded automatically on Sep 28 (255 cents).
- Admin impersonation produced a customer-style error "This action is disabled while impersonating" on Sept 26 inside the VPS wizard, which is expected behavior, not a customer problem.

## Context for the Oct 5-6 changes
- Wizard version: steps unchanged since the Sep 14 rewrite (so w1 vs w0 is comparable). The deploy wizard preselect fix for Minecraft Latest shipped Oct 5 10:50.
- Bedrock fix commit 05:24 Oct 6 (prod 05:34): no Bedrock failures for real customers after 05:31 in the data; 2 Bedrock selections this week, so volume is too small to say the fix works end to end.
- Directory v2, status notices, invoices, node-6: no signup-impacting error found in logs; I found nothing in the data tying status notices or invoice changes to conversion.
- Primary crash at 15:23 UTC: web restarted 15:28:16; 502s on /login 29, /dashboard/servers/* 48 over the week mostly on Oct 5 10:xx and Oct 6 13/15 UTC; visits and signups continued (1 signup in the 15:00 hour).
- About 989 "Server Reference ID did not match" log lines since Sep 29 are scanner traffic (bad action IDs, bursty and peaking at about 20 per hour); not customer impact, but it fills logs that make real action errors harder to see.

## Data gaps to close (so the next run can answer the questions this one could not)
1. Payment outcomes: no record of Stripe/PayPal declines, 3DS failures, abandoned Checkout sessions, or currency; all payment-failure reasons asked about were unobservable. Add events (item 3 above).
2. Wallet top-ups for non-completers and "checkout opened" count.
3. First-week panel usage (console/files logins) is not recorded per account in a form joinable to signup; I used UserSession.lastSeenAt as a proxy.
4. Visit.userId is only set once a user is logged in; attribution here is by joining on visitorId, 94 percent coverage (144 of 153).
5. "Time to verify" is about 0 for all verified email users (verification is stamped at signup), so it cannot measure friction; the unverified-forever count is the useful number.

I'm considering whether to tally human-generated 5xx errors into the existing CrawlerDaily table, but that risks polluting crawler insights with a fake "human" bot entry. It seems safer to create a separate HttpErrorDaily table instead.

Settling on a new HttpErrorDaily(date, route, status, hits) table grouped by route patterns like /login or /dashboard/deploy, which properly supports rules like "500s on deploy routes." I'm finalizing the additive schema with ErrorDaily, HttpErrorDaily, PaymentEvent, ReportView, and ReportRun tables plus several new indexes across AuditLog, EmailLog, User, Visit, WalletTransaction, Invoice, Ticket, and ErrorLog. That 81% visitor drop looks suspicious—the prior week's numbers likely included unclassified bot traffic since bot classification only started October 1st and wasn't backfilled, so the comparison period may be inflated by bots counted as humans rather than reflecting a real drop. I want to check whether visits before that date have a null bot classification to confirm this artifact.

For the payment funnel, the real issue is that completion events are recorded server-side without a sessionId, so the matching logic for "deploy funnel complete" never links back to the payment session—meaning sessions appear incomplete even when the user did complete the flow. I need to fix this by matching completions through userId instead of session ID, building a per-product set of completed users and checking if a session's user has a completion event after their payment step within the period.

Separately, the "provisioning failures rose from zero to 10" wording is awkward—I should rephrase zero-baseline cases to just say "rose from zero to N" without the "against 0" tail. The fleet alert severity labeling also needs a check since "most common" is currently picked by overall count rather than filtered to critical-severity events, which produces a misleading WARN label under a "critical" heading.

I also want to shorten the previous-period label used in sentences—something like "the previous 7 days" instead of the full verbose date range—while keeping the detailed date range available separately for cases where it's needed.

Signups (145) versus the friction report's 150 look consistent given the slightly offset date windows, so that's fine. Now I need to verify how bots are being classified and confirm the actual severity values behind the node alerts.

content.content:
ms 777 failures []
Over the last 7 days, Nxeon earned $135.54 (down 8.9% from $148.79), took 11 new orders (up 22% from 9), and gained 145 new accounts (up 53% from 95). MRR stands at $626.45. The period is still running, so comparisons use the same elapsed time.
- [warning/high] 20 critical node alerts fired in this period (most: primary CPU (CRITICAL)); 13 are still open.
    why: A node in critical state slows or stops every customer server on it.
    do: Open monitoring for that node; if it is RAM, check ballooning floors and orphaned VMs before adding hardware.
- [critical/medium] 20 of 26 sessions that reached Payment in the VPS wizard left without ordering — 77% (81% the previous 7 days).
    why: These visitors had already picked a product, plan and region. At the average first order of $14.87 that is up to $297.40 of orders not taken.
    do: Check the payment step (total shown before card entry, local payment methods for the countries in the payment-by-country table, mobile layout). 19 signed-in leavers can be contacted from the drill-down.
- [warning/high] Orders were refused for lack of node RAM 172 times; most common: "RAM guard refused node-5, node-2, node-4 for a 32768 MB VM".
    why: Each refusal is someone trying to buy a size no node could take; the customer sees a generic failure, not 'sold out'.
    do: Free or add RAM for the refused size, show 'temporarily unavailable in this region — try X' instead of a generic error, and log the userId on refusals so they can be followed up.
- [warning/medium] Provisioning failures rose to 10, from none the previous 7 days.
    why: A customer whose first server fails rarely buys again.
    do: Open the provisioning-by-game table and fix the top failing game first.
- [positive/high] Panel actions by customers rose 108% to 324, against 156 the previous 7 days.
    why: A real improvement, not noise (it clears the minimum-sample and significance checks).
    do: Note what changed so it can be repeated.
- [warning/high] 69 signups came from device "Mobile" (48% of all signups); 17 deployed and 0 paid, against 6% paying overall.
    why: If one device signs up but never orders, the order flow is probably harder on that device — not the audience.
    do: Walk the deploy wizard on a mobile screen (plan cards, region step, sticky continue button, keyboard over the button); compare the device step table in the funnel section.
- [warning/medium] 10 of 18 sessions that reached Payment in the game-server wizard left without ordering — 56% (74% the previous 7 days).
    why: These visitors had already picked a product, plan and region. At the average first order of $14.87 that is up to $148.70 of orders not taken.
    do: Check the payment step (total shown before card entry, local payment methods for the countries in the payment-by-country table, mobile layout). 9 signed-in leavers can be contacted from the drill-down.
- [warning/high] 53 signups came from landing page "/free-vps" (37% of all signups); 3 deployed and 0 paid, against 6% paying overall.
    why: A page that brings signups who never buy usually promises something the product doesn't sell (e.g. 'free VPS'), and those signups also hide the real conversion rate.
    do: Rewrite the /free-vps hero to say plainly what is free and show the cheapest paid option; consider reporting its signups separately.

#!/bin/bash
# npm prebuild/predev guard. In a live tree (/opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging)
# .next is a SYMLINK to the release the running server is serving from
# (scripts/lib/seamless-release.sh). `next build` / `next dev` there would wipe
# or rewrite that live release in place — a worse version of the 2026-10-01
# outage. Build with scripts/promote-production.sh / deploy-staging.sh instead.
if [ -L .next ]; then
  echo "REFUSING: $(pwd)/.next is a symlink to a live release ($(readlink .next))." >&2
  echo "Do not build or run next dev in a live tree. Deploy with scripts/promote-production.sh or scripts/deploy-staging.sh." >&2
  exit 1
fi

ms 819 failures []
ms 1862 failures []
Over the last 7 days, Nxeon earned $135.54 (down 8.9% from $148.79), took 11 new orders (up 22% from 9), and gained 145 new accounts (up 53% from 95). MRR stands at $626.45. The period is still running, so comparisons use the same elapsed time.
- [warning/high] 20 critical node alerts fired in this period (most: primary CPU (CRITICAL)); 14 are still open.
    why: A node in critical state slows or stops every customer server on it.
    do: Open monitoring for that node; if it is RAM, check ballooning floors and orphaned VMs before adding hardware.
- [critical/medium] 20 of 26 sessions that reached Payment in the VPS wizard left without ordering — 77% (81% the previous 7 days).
    why: These visitors had already picked a product, plan and region. At the average first order of $14.87 that is up to $297.40 of orders not taken.
    do: Check the payment step (total shown before card entry, local payment methods for the countries in the payment-by-country table, mobile layout). 19 signed-in leavers can be contacted from the drill-down.
- [warning/high] Orders were refused for lack of node RAM 172 times; most common: "RAM guard refused node-5, node-2, node-4 for a 32768 MB VM".
    why: Each refusal is someone trying to buy a size no node could take; the customer sees a generic failure, not 'sold out'.
    do: Free or add RAM for the refused size, show 'temporarily unavailable in this region — try X' instead of a generic error, and log the userId on refusals so they can be followed up.
- [warning/medium] Provisioning failures rose to 10, from none the previous 7 days.
    why: A customer whose first server fails rarely buys again.
    do: Open the provisioning-by-game table and fix the top failing game first.
- [positive/high] Panel actions by customers rose 108% to 324, against 156 the previous 7 days.
    why: A real improvement, not noise (it clears the minimum-sample and significance checks).
    do: Note what changed so it can be repeated.
- [warning/high] 69 signups came from device "Mobile" (48% of all signups); 17 deployed and 0 paid, against 6% paying overall.
    why: If one device signs up but never orders, the order flow is probably harder on that device — not the audience.
    do: Walk the deploy wizard on a mobile screen (plan cards, region step, sticky continue button, keyboard over the button); compare the device step table in the funnel section.
- [warning/medium] 10 of 18 sessions that reached Payment in the game-server wizard left without ordering — 56% (74% the previous 7 days).
    why: These visitors had already picked a product, plan and region. At the average first order of $14.87 that is up to $148.70 of orders not taken.
    do: Check the payment step (total shown before card entry, local payment methods for the countries in the payment-by-country table, mobile layout). 9 signed-in leavers can be contacted from the drill-down.
- [warning/high] 53 signups came from landing page "/free-vps" (37% of all signups); 3 deployed and 0 paid, against 6% paying overall.
    why: A page that brings signups who never buy usually promises something the product doesn't sell (e.g. 'free VPS'), and those signups also hide the real conversion rate.
    do: Rewrite the /free-vps hero to say plainly what is free and show the cheapest paid option; consider reporting its signups separately.

cd /tank/nxeon-wt-reports && grep -n "^## " docs/DOCUMENTATION.md | tail -5; cat >> docs/DOCUMENTATION.md <<'EOF'

## Automated Reports — /admin/reports (2026-10-06, branch `feature/admin-reports`)

An analyst-style report for any time frame, generated **without an LLM**: SQL aggregation + a pure, unit-tested rule engine that writes every sentence from a template. Admin only (`requireArea("analytics")` = ADMIN role; nav: Growth → Reports).

**Pages.** `/admin/reports` (time-frame picker: Today / 7d / 30d / 90d / MTD / custom, compare-to-previous toggle, time zone; executive summary of the top 5–8 findings; one section per domain with KPI tiles, narrative, charts, ranked lists, tables + per-table CSV; Print / PDF; saved views; "Save snapshot"; scheduled digest settings). `/admin/reports/drill/[kind]` (the customers/orders behind a finding: signups, unverified, unactivated, payment_leavers, orders, refunds, declines, renewal_declines, provision_failures, churned, tickets). `/admin/reports/journey/[userId]` (one customer's timeline: first-touch visit → signup → verify → wizard steps → payments → orders → provisioning → panel usage → support → emails). `/admin/reports/runs/[id]` (stored snapshot). `/admin/reports/rules` (every rule + threshold). `/admin/reports/export` (CSV; customer emails **masked** unless `unmask=1`, which is audited as `reports.export_unmasked`).

**Code.** `lib/reports/range.ts` (time zone–aware, DST-safe ranges; a running period is compared with the same elapsed time of the previous period; 4 baseline periods for anomaly detection) · `collect.ts` + `collect-growth.ts` / `collect-money.ts` / `collect-ops.ts` (SELECT-only aggregation; reuses `lib/insights/*` for MRR, earned revenue, churn, support, capacity, partners so numbers match /admin/insights; 60 s in-process cache) · `engine.ts` (change / anomaly / friction rules, ranking, headline, narrative) · `stats.ts` (significance tests with minimum samples) · `classify.ts` (channel, landing page, order kind, ticket topic, usage category, email masking, internal-account suffixes) · `drill.ts`, `journey.ts`, `digest.ts`, `activity-source.ts`, `routes.ts`, `sql.ts`. Actions: `lib/actions-reports.ts`.

**Who counts.** `realUser()` = role CUSTOMER, `excludeFromRevenue = false`, and NOT an internal e-mail suffix (`.test`, `.local`, `.invalid`, `example.*`) — the 2026-10-06 friction analysis found 17+ unflagged `@nxeon-internal.test` QA accounts polluting funnels/provisioning; the report excludes them and raises a finding until they are flagged. Visits are bot-free; a comparison period whose visits predate bot classification (before 2026-09-30, until `scripts/backfill-bot-classification.ts` runs) is not compared and a caveat is shown.

**Restraint.** Counts need ≥10 events, a ≥25 % move and z ≥ 1.96; rates need ≥20 trials per side and ≥5 points; money needs ≥5 transactions per side, ≥25 % and ≥$20; anomalies need ≥3 baseline periods and |z| ≥ 3 outside the observed range. Findings on small samples are labelled "early signal" and ranked down. Ranking = estimated cents at stake + customers affected × the average first order (real data), × severity × confidence.

**Friction rules** (each one a pattern found by hand in `/root/agent-notes/signup-friction/REPORT.md`): payment_left, payment_country, card_declines_country (+ decline reason, 3-D Secure), renewal_declines, verification_never_clicked, no_activation, dead_segment (free-intent landing page / channel / device that never pays), device_step_gap (mobile wizard drop vs desktop), device_conversion_gap, sold_out (sold-out region shown + node RAM-guard capacity refusals), provision_failed_game (by game and node), stale_provisioning (RUNNING but install step never cleared), money_path_errors (ErrorDaily + HTTP 5xx on signup/deploy/payment routes), order_validation_late, email_failures, new_error_type, support_backlog, free_mc_activation, winback_results, promo_renewals, fleet_alerts, internal_accounts.

**New data capture (all additive, best-effort, never throws).** `ErrorDaily` — per-UTC-day count per ErrorLog fingerprint, bumped by `lib/log.ts persist()` (no message/user columns). `HttpErrorDaily` — human (non-bot) HTTP 5xx per day per coarse route group, tallied by the existing access-log sweep (`lib/bots/crawler-ingest.ts`, `lib/reports/routes.ts routeGroup` collapses ids). PROVISION_FAILED deploy-funnel events now carry `detail` `{serverId, game, nodeId}` (`worker/index.ts`, `recordDeployFunnelError({detail})`). `ReportView` (saved views), `ReportRun` (snapshots/digests). Payment-attempt and page/wizard capture is **not** duplicated here: `lib/reports/activity-source.ts` reads the shared first-party activity table from `lib/activity-events.ts` (branch `feature/signup-fixes-activity`) when it exists — discovering its table/columns at runtime — and the payments section / journey say "appears once activity-event capture is deployed" until then. Additive indexes: AuditLog(action, createdAt)/(userId, createdAt)/(createdAt), EmailLog(createdAt)/(userId, createdAt)/(template, createdAt), User(createdAt), Visit(userId, createdAt), WalletTransaction(createdAt)/(userId, createdAt), Invoice(userId)/(createdAt), Ticket(userId)/(createdAt), ErrorLog(firstSeen).

**Scheduled digest** (default OFF): settings `report_digest_enabled` (false), `report_digest_frequency` (daily = yesterday, weekly = last Mon–Sun), `report_digest_to` (blank → `reports_email`), `report_digest_tz`. `lib/reports/digest.ts reportDigestSweep` runs hourly from `worker/analytics.ts`, after 06:00 local, once per period (ReportRun `emailedAt`). The email contains no customer e-mail addresses.

**Deploy.** `npm run db:push` (additive tables + indexes; the index builds briefly lock the small tables), `npx prisma generate` in `/opt/nxeon`, then the normal staging → promote flow; restart the worker for the digest sweep (inert until enabled). Tests: `test/reports-engine.test.ts`, `test/reports-range.test.ts`, `test/reports-digest.test.ts`, `test/reports-rbac.test.ts`, `test/reports-collect-db.test.ts` (throwaway DB via `REPORTS_TEST_DATABASE_URL`).

**Not covered yet.** Checkout opened/cancelled/declined (waits on the activity-event table); panel file-manager/SFTP usage (not audited); bounces after SMTP acceptance; sold-out exposure in the wizard (waits on activity capture); per-event ErrorDaily history before deploy (falls back to ErrorLog lifetime counts, labelled).
EOF

Adds ErrorDaily, HttpErrorDaily, ReportView, ReportRun + additive indexes. See "Automated Reports" near the end of this document.\n'

## What was built
Branch `feature/admin-reports` in worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-reports`, two commits on top of main b23bc8e8d5:
- `f2a096e225`: data capture, schema and indexes.
- `08f202bdc5`: the /admin/reports feature, its tests and docs.

It is not merged and not deployed. The post-commit hook auto-pushed the branch to origin. Prod was only read: I used a read-only connection (`default_transaction_read_only=on`), and a test write against it was refused with error 25006. I followed your mid-task note: I removed the payment-event and wizard capture I had started. Reports now read the other agent's activity-event table through `lib/reports/activity-source.ts`, which finds the table and its columns at runtime and shows "appears once activity-event capture is deployed" while it is missing. No LLM is called anywhere; every sentence comes from a template.

## Pages (admin only)
- **`/admin/reports`**
  - Time-frame picker: Today, 7d, 30d, 90d, MTD, custom range, a compare-to-previous toggle and a time zone.
  - An executive summary of the top 5–8 findings. Each says what happened (with the number and the comparison), why it matters and what to do, has a link to the affected customers, and is marked "early signal" when the sample is small.
  - One section per area, each with KPI tiles, a short written paragraph, charts, ranked lists, tables and a CSV per table: Acquisition, Signups, Deploy funnel, Orders & revenue, Payments, Provisioning, Product usage, Retention & churn, Support, Errors, Fleet & capacity, Email.
  - Print/PDF, saved views, "Save snapshot", and the scheduled digest settings.
- **`/admin/reports/drill/[kind]`** lists the people or orders behind a finding: signups, unverified, unactivated, payment leavers, orders, refunds, declines, renewal declines, provision failures, churned, tickets.
- **`/admin/reports/journey/[userId]`** is one customer's timeline: first visit and channel → signup → verify → wizard steps → payments → orders → provisioning → panel use → support → emails.
- **`/admin/reports/runs/[id]`** shows saved snapshots; **`/admin/reports/rules`** lists every rule and threshold.
- **CSV exports** mask emails (j***@gmail.com) unless `unmask=1` is passed, and that is audit-logged. Card data is never shown.

## Rules
- **Change and anomaly checks on every metric.** A finding is only raised when the sample is big enough:
  - Counts: at least 10 events, a 25% move, and a significance test (z ≥ 1.96).
  - Rates: at least 20 trials on each side and a 5-point move.
  - Money: at least 5 transactions on each side and at least $20.
  - Anomalies: outside the range of the 4 previous equal periods, with |z| ≥ 3.
  - A period still in progress is compared with the same elapsed time of the previous one.
- **22 friction rules**, taken from the hand-run REPORT.md:
  - `payment_left`, `payment_country`
  - `card_declines_country` (also decline reason and 3-D Secure)
  - `renewal_declines`, `verification_never_clicked`, `no_activation`
  - `dead_segment` (a free-intent landing page, channel or device that never pays)
  - `device_step_gap` (mobile wizard drop vs desktop), `device_conversion_gap`
  - `sold_out` (sold-out region shown, plus node-RAM capacity refusals)
  - `provision_failed_game` (by game and by node), `stale_provisioning`
  - `money_path_errors` (errors and HTTP 5xx on signup/deploy/payment), `order_validation_late`
  - `email_failures`, `new_error_type`, `support_backlog`, `free_mc_activation`
  - `winback_results`, `promo_renewals`, `fleet_alerts`, `internal_accounts`

## Sample summary from real prod data (last 7 days, Sep 30 – Oct 6 17:45 UTC; took 0.8 s, 30 days took 1.9 s)
"Over the last 7 days, Nxeon earned $135.54 (down 8.9% from $148.79), took 11 new orders (up 22% from 9), and gained 145 new accounts (up 53% from 95). MRR stands at $626.45."
1. 20 critical node alerts this period (most: primary CPU); 14 still open.
2. 20 of 26 sessions that reached Payment in the VPS wizard left without ordering, 77% (81% the week before); 19 signed-in leavers are listed.
3. Orders were refused 172 times for lack of node RAM, most often "RAM guard refused node-5, node-2, node-4 for a 32768 MB VM".
4. Provisioning failures rose to 10, from none the previous 7 days (Bedrock 3, Valheim 3; node-2 60% of attempts).
5. Customer panel actions rose 108% to 324 (good news).
6. 69 signups came from Mobile (48% of all signups); 17 deployed and 0 paid, against 6% paying overall.
7. 10 of 18 game-wizard Payment sessions left, 56% (74% the week before).
8. 53 signups came from /free-vps (37%); 3 deployed and 0 paid.

Further down:
- 6 of 25 email signups never verified.
- 32 free Minecraft servers were created; only 6 were ever joined by a player and 0 of their owners pay.
- deploy_winback went to 64 people: 2 clicked, 3 came back.
- 1 renewal was declined for insufficient funds.
- 19 internal QA accounts are not flagged "exclude from revenue".

I checked by direct SQL that signups (145) and revenue earned ($135.54) match. Payment-step and mobile/free-vps numbers line up with REPORT.md.

Data caveat the page shows: visitor numbers before Sep 30 were never bot-classified, so visitor comparisons are switched off until `scripts/backfill-bot-classification.ts` is run.

## Things you should know
- **19 QA accounts are counted as customers elsewhere.** Accounts at `@nxeon-internal.test` / `.local` have role CUSTOMER and are not flagged `excludeFromRevenue`. Reports exclude them; other admin pages still count them. Flag them.
- **Two existing test failures are not from this branch.** `test/admin-console-guards.test.ts` tests 13 and 14 fail on `app/admin/page.tsx`; they fail the same way with my changes stashed.

## Tests
- `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- 39 new tests pass: `reports-engine` (thresholds, minimum samples, period comparison, every friction rule, ranking), `reports-range` (time zones, DST, partial periods, caps), `reports-digest`, `reports-rbac` (admin-only, every page and action guarded, emails masked), and `reports-collect-db` (aggregation SQL against a throwaway Postgres: real-customer filter, funnel matched by user, money, ErrorDaily, a time-zone boundary). Alongside them I ran the error-log, bot-classify and insights-stats tests: no new failures. 
- The full suite was not run because of the memory rule.
- The UI was checked on a dev server (:3131) with synthetic data, at desktop and 390 px: all pages return 200, no page errors, no horizontal scroll; CSV and print-to-PDF work; a logged-out visitor is redirected to login.

Screenshots and the PDF are in `/root/agent-notes/admin-reports/`. The dev server, throwaway database, `.env` and `.next` were all removed; the worktree keeps its own non-symlinked `node_modules`.

## Deploy steps
1. Merge, then `npm run db:push`. It adds `ErrorDaily`, `HttpErrorDaily`, `ReportView`, `ReportRun` and the extra indexes; the index builds briefly lock small tables.
2. Run `npx prisma generate` in `/opt/nxeon` itself.
3. Deploy with `deploy-staging.sh`, then `promote-production.sh`.
4. Restart the worker. The digest job is hourly and stays inert until switched on in the Reports page; it is off by default.
5. Optionally run the bot-classification backfill so visitor history can be compared.

## Not covered yet
- Checkout opened/cancelled/declined and sold-out exposure in the wizard: these wait on the activity-event table.
- File-manager/SFTP use is not in the audit log.
- Bounces after the mail server accepts a message are not visible.
- Per-day error counts start at deploy; before that, errors show lifetime counts, labelled as such.
- HTTP 5xx counts start at deploy (no backfill).
- The monthly cohort table needs more paying history.

Docs: a new "Automated Reports" section and a change-history entry in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.
